EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS ON AMAZON FINE FOOD REVIEWS¶

Introduction¶

The digital environment strongly depends on online reviews because produce customer perception changes and business directive shifts. Amazon and other companies collect massive amounts of user-generated reviews that supply useful market insights for product quality assessments, customer satisfaction metrics, and marketplace trends. The research tackles Explanatory Data Analysis (EDA) through the exploration of the Amazon Fine Food Reviews dataset. This dataset contains 568,454 user-generated reviews of various food items which include user ratings together with review text and ratings of helpfulness. The movement aims to obtain valuable business knowledge through driven decision recommendations.

Data Exploration¶

The dataset contains 568,454 customer reviews spread across 10 features which encompass product details together with user information and their reviews and rating data. The initial analysis of the dataset showed the existence of multiple quality problems within its data (Josse et al. 2024). The ProfileName column contains 16 missing values and 27 entries are missing values from the Summary column. Users who have submitted multiple reviews about the same product created duplicate entries in the review data. The review system checks UserId and ProductId parameters together with Text content to detect these duplicates (Poonguzhali et al. 2022). Some instances have revealed problems with inconsistent helpfulness scores because HelpfulnessNumerator exceeded HelpfulnessDenominator. The Time column contains Unix timestamp values which need to be converted into a readable format because they currently lack human-readable measurement. The dataset requires cleaning and structuring procedures as a prerequisite for performing meaningful analysis because of its observed poor data quality.

Data Preprocessing¶

Data preprocessing has concentrated on enhancing data quality through the resolution of multiple problems (Maharana et al. 2022). The review dataset has undergone a process to eliminate duplication because every review entry must remain distinct. Helpfulness scores received normalization treatment so the HelpfulnessNumerator does not exceed the HelpfulnessDenominator values (Zhang et al. 2023). The dataset includes appropriate placeholder values to handle empty values among the ProfileName and Summary fields. The Time attribute now displays relevant date information instead of Unix timestamp values. Through these preprocessing methods, the data preparation work achieved a standardized dataset that permits precise analysis to generate significant data-driven conclusions.

Remove duplicate¶

In [106]:
# Remove duplicate reviews
df.drop_duplicates(subset=["UserId", "ProductId", "Text"], keep="first", inplace=True)

# Fix inconsistent helpfulness scores
df = df[df["HelpfulnessNumerator"] <= df["HelpfulnessDenominator"]]

# Handle missing values by filling them with default values
df["ProfileName"] = df["ProfileName"].fillna("Unknown")
df["Summary"] = df["Summary"].fillna("No Summary")


# Convert timestamps to readable date format
df["Time"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Time"], unit="s")

# Display updated dataset info
df.info()

1. What Are the Most Reviewed Products?¶

Analytical evaluation reveals that the most reviewed products exist and the top-rated product obtained 913 reviews. These popular items have generated considerable customer interest because of high customer demand. The identified products enable businesses to boost their marketing plans by leveraging reviews for higher customer satisfaction.

In [111]:
# Count the number of reviews per product
reviews_per_product = df["ProductId"].value_counts()

# Plot histogram
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.hist(reviews_per_product, bins=50, color="green", edgecolor="black", alpha=0.7)

# Labels and title
plt.title("Distribution of Number of Reviews Per Product", fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel("Number of Reviews", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Frequency (Number of Products)", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)

# Show the plot
plt.show()

2. What Is the Distribution of Review Scores?¶

Review scores show a bias toward positive ratings because 5-star ratings appear most frequently according to the analysis. Customer dissatisfaction appears less frequently in 1-star reviews even though these reviews are less common than positive 5-star submissions. These findings help employees view overall customer happiness and satisfaction patterns.

In [114]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Count the number of reviews per score
score_distribution = df["Score"].value_counts().sort_index()

# Plot the distribution
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
score_distribution.plot(kind="bar", color="skyblue", edgecolor="black")
plt.title("Distribution of Review Scores", fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel("Review Score", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Number of Reviews", fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=0)
plt.grid(axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)
plt.show()

3. Which Products Have the Highest Average Rating?¶

The analysis obtained highest-rated products through a computation of product average ratings. Multiple reviews indicate that items ranked as highly rated consistently demonstrate excellent satisfaction levels from customers. High-quality products from the analysis have received recognition enabling businesses to market them successfully while boosting customer acquisition along with sales growth.

In [117]:
# Calculate average rating per product and get the top 10
top_rated_products = df.groupby("ProductId")["Score"].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10)

# Plot pie chart
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.pie(top_rated_products, labels=top_rated_products.index, autopct="%1.1f%%", 
        colors=plt.cm.Paired.colors, startangle=140)

# Title
plt.title("Top 10 Highest Rated Products", fontsize=14)

# Show the plot
plt.show()

4. Are Longer Reviews More Helpful?¶

Review length determines the number of helpfulness votes received by reviews according to the analysis. The data reveals that reviews holding lengthy lengths tend to generate greater helpfulness votes among customers who deem detailed explanations beneficial. The observed trend enhances the critical importance of offering thorough feedback to achieve stronger audience involvement and enhance credibility ratings.

In [22]:
# Create a new column for review length
df["ReviewLength"] = df["Text"].apply(len)

# Scatter plot of review length vs. helpfulness votes
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.scatterplot(x=df["ReviewLength"], y=df["HelpfulnessNumerator"], alpha=0.3)
plt.title("Review Length vs. Helpfulness Votes", fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel("Review Length (characters)", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Helpfulness Votes", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)
plt.show()

5. How Do Review Scores Change Over Time?¶

The research demonstrates that average review ratings have displayed consistent patterns throughout the study. Minimal changes have been detected in the series while the number of reviews has largely been stable. The stability of overall customer satisfaction levels shows businesses can improve their strategies confidently since there is no danger of falling product ratings.

In [123]:
# Extract year from the timestamp
df["Year"] = df["Time"].dt.year

# Calculate average score per year
yearly_avg_score = df.groupby("Year")["Score"].mean()

# Plot trend over time
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
yearly_avg_score.plot(marker="o", color="blue", linestyle="-")
plt.title("Average Review Score Over Time", fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel("Year", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Average Score", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)
plt.show()

6. What Words Are Most Common in 5-Star vs. 1-Star Reviews?¶

Word cloud analysis uncovered the most predominant words utilized within both 5-star and 1-star rating reviews. Customers indicate their satisfaction through expressions of love and descriptions of the meal as both great and delicious. Various negative reviews contain words including "bad" "disappointed" and "waste" which demonstrate customer dissatisfaction. The identified customer sentiments have enabled businesses to target specific product problems through appropriate solutions.

In [126]:
# Function to generate word clouds for different ratings
def generate_wordcloud(score):
    text = " ".join(df[df["Score"] == score]["Text"])
    wordcloud = WordCloud(width=800, height=400, background_color="white").generate(text)

    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
    plt.imshow(wordcloud, interpolation="bilinear")
    plt.axis("off")
    plt.title(f"Most Common Words in {score}-Star Reviews", fontsize=14)
    plt.show()

# Generate word clouds for 1-star and 5-star reviews
generate_wordcloud(1)
generate_wordcloud(5)

7. Who Are the Top Reviewers?¶

By counting user reviews the analysis has established the leading reviewers within the platform. User engagement stands higher in those individuals who have written many reviews than other users. A select group of review writers has effectively formed how customers view products and maintained their trustworthiness. Through these insights, businesses improved their products while using them in their marketing campaigns.

Conclusion¶

The conducted exploratory data analysis revealed important customer data together with product popularity results and review trend patterns. The research outcomes have revealed which products gained the most reviews and achieved maximum customer ratings making them the most popular choices among shoppers. The scoring distribution shows a larger volume of positive reviews and the sentiment analysis discovered major positive and negative vocabulary in the reviews. Businesses have used stable rating trends to optimize their operational strategies. The analysis of helpfulness votes shows that detailed feedback produces better outcomes from review length perspective. The research provides companies with data-based tools to strengthen customer satisfaction and improve marketing techniques for improving product placement and audience engagement.
